item.title: 2nd Friday ArtWalk: Acktoberfest — Fri Oct 9, 5:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description: Join us for the Ackland Art Museum’s fifth annual Acktoberfest — an evening filled with art, crafts, and local vendors! Art supplies will be available in our ART& space, where visitors can create their own paper plants inspired by Phaan Howng: Against Nature. There will also be postcards inspired by the installation for visitors to enjoy and use. Explore our special exhibitions Care and Concern: Recent Acquisitions of Modern and Contemporary Art , and Continental Shift: Recent Acquisitions of African Art throughout the evening with extended museum hours. Local vendors will be on hand with goods to browse and purchase, including Dingo Dog Brewing Company, where visitors can grab a drink to sip while crafting. Acktoberfest is a free, walk-in program; no registration required to attend or craft. Museum galleries will be open from 5–9 p.m.; the vendors will be onsite from 6–8:30 p.m. Our vendors: Dingo Dog Brewing Flower of Carolina Nailah’s Shea Student Made UNC Word and Plant

item.title: JIM MCKEON: DURHAM SWEET DURHAM — Sat Oct 10, 1:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description: 5 Points Gallery is proud to present Durham Sweet Durham, a new exhibition of oil paintings by Featured Artist Jim McKeon celebrating the vibrant soul of the Bull City through crisp realism and touches of fantasy. From historic brick warehouses to the wild banks of the Eno River, familiar Durham landscapes become evocative scenes of memory, community, and place. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our ten Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, September 18, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artist. Durham Sweet Durham runs from September 17 through October 10, 2026. Image: 4th of July, Bulls Stadium, oil on canvas, 90 × 66 inches. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. item.title: Close Up Foundation Next Gen - A DAY OF DELIBERATIVE DIALOGUE — Tue Oct 13, 8:00 AM — None
item.description:
On October 13, 2026, Close Up will lead a regional deliberation at Duke University. This event is one of six regional deliberations taking place in 2026-27 across the country as part of NextGen Roundtable: America 250, a growing initiative to honor the Semiquincentennial of the United States. Through civil discourse, we aim to empower students to engage in meaningful dialogue, listen with empathy, and express their ideas with clarity and confidence.
This NextGen Roundtable regional deliberation will convene up to 250 high school students from public, charter, private, and independent schools in the area who represent a cross-section of backgrounds and perspectives. Students will deliberate on economic policy issues in small groups moderated by neutral facilitators, weigh diverse perspectives from their peers and a panel of policy experts, and craft vision statements for making an impact in their community. All participating students will receive Close Up's Deliberative Dialogue Badge

item.title: Learning in Networks Reading Group — Tue Oct 13, 12:00 PM — Gross Hall
item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. By fostering collaboration across disciplines, the institute aims to develop new mathematical and algorithmic foundations for understanding complex networked systems and their applications. The institute is led by collaborators Jiaming Xu, Alex Belloni, Fan Wei, Galen Reeves, and James Moody. Learn more: https://sites.duke.edu/learninginnetworks/

item.title: ecoEXPLORE Shifting Species: Climate & Behavior and Arachnid Costume Party (Columbia) — Tue Oct 27, 3:30 PM
item.description: Can you think of ways that wildlife might respond to changes in climate? During our ecoEXPLORE “Shifting Species” program, NCWF, Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge, and Tyrrell County Library will dive into how species shift their behavior in response to changes in weather vs. climate as we work to complete our Climate Badge Challenge 3! Join us as we learn more about local and regional examples of wildlife and plants that have adapted due to changes in their environment. To celebrate the end of the Arachnology Field Season, ecoEXPLORErs are invited to wear their arachnid costumes from the Arachnology Badge Challenge 3! Don’t feel like dressing up? That’s okay, we’d love to see a sketch of your costume design instead! ecoEXPLORE is a community science program, created by the North Carolina Arboretum, where children of all ages are able to learn how to identify wildlife around them, help real scientists track wildlife activity, and earn fun badges and prizes all at the same time!

item.title: Mesh-LLM & Trusting a Stranger's Machine, Part 2: Evidence You Can Check — Mon Oct 12, 5:00 PM
item.description:
All Things AI (Live) When a stranger's machine serves an AI request, how can the requester check what happened? We'll show mesh-llm's Evidence plugin recording signed, hash-chained evidence on each node and sending each side's signed record to the other.
A demo build will show both-sides confirmation and a paid Lightning exchange; we'll label the build and distinguish it from a released version. I'll show a TRACE record alongside the exchange capsule to explain what additional runtime evidence, including hardware evidence when available, can establish. We'll also show the limits: the plugin's node keys are self-attested, and its referee applies once mesh-llm marks twins.
